title: Introduce credential-rotor and lightweight stream retry shim across Python/TS/Go SDKs
author: Maya Liu
release_notes: Adds a cross-SDK credential rotor and compact stream retry shim. SDKs: Py v2.3.0, TS v1.9.0, Go v1.6.0. Backward-compatible; recommends opt-in via config. Improved streaming reconnect reliability and reduced token refresh thundering by ~3x.
description:
Motivation: credential rotation and streaming reconnects are frequent sources of transient failures and operator complexity when customers run long-lived streams across multiple SDKs. This change introduces a small, cross-language "credential rotor" primitive plus a compact retry shim for streaming consumers to reduce windowed token thrashing and improve ergonomics for callers. The goal is backwards compatible: defaults are conservative and customers opt-in via SDK config or env var.

What I changed (summary):
- Added a credential-rotor interface and reference implementations in Python/TypeScript/Go that expose: lease acquisition, soft-commit, optimistic swap, and graceful fallback to previous token until drain.
- Implemented a lightweight streaming retry shim (PullStreamAdapter) that co-ordinates rotor handoffs, de-duplicates concurrent refreshes, and applies an exponential jittered backoff tuned for typical LLM token windows.
- Bumped SDK package versions and updated changelogs and migration notes.
- End-to-end tests that exercise rotation during streaming, race conditions, and cold-start behavior.
- Docs + short example snippets for each SDK showing opt-in config and recommended patterns.

Key design notes (single-line descriptions):
- Rotor leases default to 60s with a swap_threshold 0.35 (optimistic swap when 35% lease elapsed); configurable per-SDK.
- De-duplication uses an in-process singleflight per credential key; inter-process coordination is out of scope (recommended for Private deployments to use external KVS).
- The shim is intentionally minimal: it wraps existing stream consumption APIs and exposes a small callback for token refresh events so callers can plug their own telemetry.

Files touched (high-level):
- sdk/python/redwood/auth/rotor.py (new)
- sdk/python/redwood/stream/adapter.py (changes)
- sdk/typescript/src/auth/rotor.ts (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/compact-shim.ts (new)
- sdk/go/auth/rotor.go (new)
- sdk/go/stream/shim.go (new)
- docs/sdk/rotor.md (new)
- tests/integ/rotor_streaming.py (new), rotor_streaming.ts, rotor_streaming_go.go

Checklist: implemented, tested, documented, bumped versions, and added migration notes.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: subtle races during parallel refresh; mitigations: singleflight per-key and unit tests that simulate concurrent refresh with mock time.
- Risk: customers relying on existing token lifecycle semantics might see different timing; mitigations: config opt-in and clear migration docs.

Related: references ENG-8240 (design doc), SUP-412 (customer incident that motivated this), and several cross-sdk streaming parity PRs.
